subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
MWCC GC 1.2.5 family. ON A RESPELL THAT MOVES LOOP-INVARIANT FP CONSTANTS BETWEEN POINT-OF-USE AND CALLEE-SAVED-HOIST, BOTH `real` AND COUNT DISTANCE INVERT THE FUZZY RANKING, AND FUZZY IS THE ONLY ARBITER THAT SURVIVES. Four forms of one function, each fully rebuilt and freshly scored, ranked by fuzzy against ranked by real:

  form                                          insns(T/O)  count-dist  multiset  real   fuzzy
  F  5 hoisted constants, 5th via manual inline  445/453      8          8t       438   92.4742  <- BEST fuzzy
  A  four f64 literal initializers (baseline)    445/453      8          8t       446   92.0225
  C' named externs bound to inner-block locals   445/453      8          8t       446   91.9483
  E  C' + gCameraTargets as a blob displacement  445/452      7          7t       587   91.3056
  B  bare extern reads at point of use           445/454      9          9t       435   90.2180  <- BEST real

THE INVERSION IS THE POINT. Form B carries the roster's LOWEST `real` (435, eleven better than baseline) and its WORST fuzzy (90.22, a 1.8-point REGRESSION); a real-ordered queue banks it and ships a regression. Form E carries the BEST count distance (7) and the best multiset (7t) and is the second-worst fuzzy; the run-27 probe.py amendment's advice to weight count distance over the multiset on a CONFLICT verdict points at E, which is also wrong. Only fuzzy ordered these correctly, and it did so on all five.

WHY, and this is what makes it predictable rather than folklore: `real` counts differing rows in a positional alignment, so it is dominated by WHERE a surplus instruction sits, not by how many there are. Form B deletes the four hoisted lfd from the entry region -- the densest, most-aligned part of the function -- which lets the aligner pair the entry cleanly and drops ~11 rows, while scattering one reload into each of five loop bodies where the aligner absorbs them silently. objdiff's fuzzy weights the whole body and sees the five scattered reloads for what they are. Corollary: any edit whose effect is to MOVE instructions between a dense entry region and a loop body will move `real` in the wrong direction, and the size of the `real` swing is not evidence about the size of the code change -- form E's +141 `real` came from removing TWO instructions.

OPERATIONAL RULE. On a hoist-vs-reload respell, or any edit that relocates instructions across the entry/loop boundary, do not arbitrate on probe.py's verdict at all: probe called form B IMPROVED and form E CONFLICT-with-better-count-distance, and both were regressions. Spend the full ninja and read fuzzy from the fresh report. This is the unequal-count extension of claim.law.EN-equal-count-opcode-respell-must-be-arbitrated-on-fuzzy-not-real, which had scoped the fuzzy-arbitration rule to the equal-count case only; here counts differed by one in both directions and fuzzy was still the only reliable signal. The cost is one full build per form, and on this function it was the difference between a +0.45 fuzzy commit and a -1.81 fuzzy commit.
